entries.provenance: External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, ungated). The repo ships no litertlm_manifest.json; backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate. The bundle's structured template pre-opens the think block (<think> followed by a newline) and declares no channel, so handler_config.channels declares it: the runtime then starts the capture on the prompt and diverts the reasoning into Message.channels.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. A hybrid attention / Mamba-2 model: the bundle declares fp32 activations for the GPU, and the manifest lists gpu and cpu as verified to generate.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json; the bundle declares a <think> channel in its template, which the runtime handles; the SDK does not enable thinking.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. A thinking model: the bundle declares the <think> channel and its generation prompt ends bare, so the model emits the opener itself; handler_config.channels spells the same channel so the SDK applies it to every conversation and reports the reasoning in Message.channels.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The vision encoder does not compile on the Pixel GPU delegate, so the gpu profile runs the language graph on the GPU and the vision encoder on the CPU (litertlm-chat-android, Pixel 8a, 2026-08-13).

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The vision encoder runs on the CPU in every profile, as for LFM2.5-VL-1.6B, whose encoder does not compile on the Pixel GPU delegate; the language graph runs on the GPU in the gpu profile.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The vision encoder runs on the CPU in every profile, as for LFM2.5-VL-1.6B, whose encoder does not compile on the Pixel GPU delegate; the language graph runs on the GPU in the gpu profile.
Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json; one int4 (block 32) file with a 4096-token context.

External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, ungated). The q8 / 4096-token file is the one on-device-recipes verified on a Pixel 8a (LiteRT-LM 0.16.1, 2026-09-05); the f32 file (6.2 GB) is left out on purpose.

External descriptor for a mixed repo (litert-community/Qwen3-0.6B, ungated, no litertlm_manifest.json): backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate. Qwen3 thinks by default (its template renders the no-think variant only when enable_thinking is false). The int4 file declares the thought channel in its own header; the mixed_int4 file does not, so handler_config.channels spells it for both.

External descriptor for a mixed repo (litert-community/Qwen3-1.7B, ungated, no litertlm_manifest.json): backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate. Qwen3 thinks by default. The int4 file declares the thought channel in its own header; the int8 file does not, so handler_config.channels spells it for both.

External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, ungated). The repo ships no litertlm_manifest.json, so backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate; the bundle's own header declares no channel and its template has no think block (an instruct model).

External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/Qwen3-4B, ungated, no litertlm_manifest.json): backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate. Qwen3 thinks by default and the bundle declares no channel, so handler_config.channels spells it. The 5.7 GB int8 file is left out: it does not fit the 8 GB phone the gate runs on.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The packaged chat template closes the think block in the generation prompt, so the model answers without reasoning and no channel is declared; the vl_int8 variant adds the vision encoder (fp16) with the encoder kept on the CPU until a GPU run is verified.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The packaged chat template closes the think block in the generation prompt, so the model answers without reasoning and no channel is declared; the vl_int8 variant adds the vision encoder (fp16, static 512x512) with the encoder kept on the CPU until a GPU run is verified.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The packaged chat template closes the think block in the generation prompt, so the model answers without reasoning and no channel is declared. The int8 file (4.4 GB) is listed for devices with more memory; the default is the mixed int4 file.

External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm, ungated on 2026-09-07). The SDK points at the repo's own file at this commit; it does not re-host it. Profiles were verified on a Pixel 8a with the SDK's catalog gate (see verification/). The bundle declares its thought channel (<|channel>thought ... <channel|>) in its own header; it is spelled here so the descriptor is complete. Gemma 4 does not reason unless thinking is enabled, so no thinking_default.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The bundle uses the structured (non-jinja) template and declares no channel.
Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. A Japanese / English instruct model on the structured template; no channel.
